title: Universal Life Insurance Interest Convention: Earnings Credited on Refunded Guideline Excess
content:
The earnings credited on guideline excess refunded from an Ashgrove Universal Life Insurance policy are figured on the guideline excess at the earnings rate plus the late-refund addition, for the days from the earnings start date to the earnings end date, and are returned with the excess in the guideline excess refund. The method follows the days since the excess payment (the most recent premium payment in the activity history) was received, counted to the refund date.

## Convention

| Days since the excess payment was received | Method of figuring the earnings |
|---|---|
| **45** or more (the compounding days) | The rate is compounded monthly over the whole thirty-day months in the earnings period (one twelfth of the annual rate per month), and the remaining days earn simple interest over 365 on the compounded amount; the earnings are the compounded amount less the excess |
| 1 to 44 | Simple interest over 365 for the earnings days |
| 0 (received on the refund date) | No earnings |

The guideline excess refund is the guideline excess plus the earnings credited on it, rounded to the cent once at the end; the earnings are not rounded on their own.

## Worked figures (hypothetical)

*Compounded.* Excess $18000.00 received 63 days ago; annual rate 6.25%; 59 earnings days, which are one whole thirty-day month and 29 remaining days. One month compounds $18000.00 by one plus 0.0625 divided by 12; the 29 days then earn simple interest of 0.0625 times 29 over 365 on that amount. The compounded amount is $18183.5991; earnings $183.5991; refund $18183.60.

*Simple.* Excess $18000.00 received 40 days ago, annual rate 5.25%, 40 earnings days: $18000.00 times 0.0525 times 40 over 365 is $103.5616; refund $18103.56.

*Same day.* Excess received on the refund date: no earnings; refund $18000.00.
